articles.title: SafeCommit: Certifying When Memory-Grounded Agents May Safely Act
articles.abstract: Long-horizon agents increasingly use persistent memory and tools to take actions with external side effects. A central failure mode is premature commitment: an agent acts before resolving whether its memory grounding is stale, conflicting, incomplete, or corrupted. We formalize this problem as safe commitment under memory uncertainty and introduce SafeCommit, a risk controlled layer between agent reasoning and external execution. The layer constructs a calibrated set of plausible latent worlds from memory, observations, tool outputs, provenance, and policy constraints. It permits a side effectful action only when a conformal action certificate shows that the action is safe in every retained world. Otherwise, it selects a low-side-effect probe that targets the worlds blocking certification, or returns a conservative fallback. Under calibrated world coverage, the probability of an unsafe certified commit is at most the target level α; with imperfect world proposal, the bound separates calibration and representation error. A dependency-free controlled simulator illustrates the safety-utility tradeoff and reproduces all reported results with one command. The goal is to offer a concrete approach for deciding not only what an agent should do, but when the available evidence is sufficient to safely do it.

articles.titleCn: SafeCommit：认证内存基础智能体何时可以安全行动
articles.abstractCn: 长时程智能体越来越多地使用持久记忆和工具来执行具有外部副作用的操作。一个核心的失效模式是过早承诺：智能体在未解决其记忆基础是否过时、冲突、不完整或损坏之前就采取行动。我们将此问题形式化为记忆不确定下的安全承诺，并引入SafeCommit，这是一个在智能体推理和外部执行之间控制风险的层。该层从记忆、观察、工具输出、溯源和政策约束中构建一组校准的潜在世界。只有当符合性操作证书表明该操作在所有保留的世界中都安全时，它才允许具有副作用的操作。否则，它选择一个低副作用探测，针对阻碍认证的世界，或返回保守的回退方案。在校准世界覆盖范围内，不安全认证承诺的概率最多为目标水平α；在非完美世界提议下，界限将校准和表示误差分开。一个无依赖的受控模拟器说明了安全性与效用之间的权衡，并使用一条命令重现了所有报告的结果。目标是提供一个具体的方法，不仅决定智能体应该做什么，而且当可用证据足够安全地执行时，决定何时执行。

articles.title: Eliciting Intrinsic Hallucinations in LLMs via Semantically Equivalent Adversarial Attacks
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are often used in conjunction with external knowledge sources to improve their factual accuracy and decrease hallucinations, through methods such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). However, these systems remain susceptible to intrinsic hallucinations, where the model generates unfaithful or fabricated information that is not supported by the retrieved evidence. We propose a novel framework to assess model robustness against this phenomenon by stress-testing using natural, semantically equivalent variations of a user query found via adversarial optimization methods. We apply our framework, which enforces strict semantic equivalence constraints and an intrinsic hallucination objective, to a range of adversarial attack techniques across white-box, gray-box, and black-box adversarial settings. Evaluating these attacks on 5 open-source and 5 closed-source generator models across 3 datasets, we demonstrate that even state-of-the-art models are highly susceptible to meaning-preserving perturbations, which significantly degrade contextual faithfulness (by up to 50% for GPT-5-mini). Our findings indicate that faithful use of in-context evidence remains fragile even in state-of-the-art LLMs, motivating architectures and training objectives that enforce robust grounding independent of surface query form. Code is available at: https://github.com/atriviveksharma/intrinsic_hall
articles.titleCn: 通过语义等价对抗攻击在大型语言模型中诱发内在幻觉
articles.abstractCn: 大型语言模型（LLMs）通常通过与外部知识源结合，并采用检索增强生成（RAG）等方法来提高其事实准确性并减少幻觉。然而，这些系统仍然容易受到内在幻觉的影响，即模型生成未经检索证据支持的不忠实或虚构信息。我们提出了一种新的框架，通过对抗优化方法找到用户查询的自然语义等效变体进行压力测试，以评估模型对此现象的鲁棒性。我们将该框架应用于白盒、灰盒和黑盒对抗设置中的多种对抗攻击技术，该框架强制执行严格的语义等价约束和内在幻觉目标。在3个数据集上对5个开源和5个闭源生成模型进行的攻击评估表明，即使是最先进的模型也极易受到保持语义的扰动，这会显著降低上下文忠实度（对GPT-5-mini的影响高达50%）。我们的研究结果表明，即使在最先进的LLMs中，对上下文证据的忠实使用仍然很脆弱，这促使我们设计能够独立于表面查询形式强制执行鲁棒基础架构和训练目标。代码可在以下链接获取：https://github.com/atriviveksharma/intrinsic_hall

articles.title: LLM-based Vulnerability Discovery in Business Process Documentation
articles.abstract: Just like software and hardware, business processes are susceptible to vulnerabilities that can lead to product quality issues, delays, and increased costs. Business process vulnerabilities can arise from a variety of sources, including conflicting requirements, ambiguous documentation, invalid measurement spec-ifications, omission of quality checks, or implementations that differ from speci-fications. MIRABELLE is a system that identifies and characterizes business logic (BL) vulnerabilities from available business process representations, in-cluding ISO 9000/9001 documentation, user guides, work instructions, and pro-cess execution logs. MIRABELLE leverages recent advances in AI/ML to pro-cess available business process documentation and generate attributed graph rep-resentations of the business logic that can be processed using both graph and for-mal logic approaches for identifying potential vulnerabilities. However, extract-ing the business logic (e.g., operation execution sequences, decisions, input/out-put resources) from mostly natural language artifacts is challenging due to the required domain expertise, inherent process complexity, and the sometimes very large volumes of information. This paper focuses on our experimentation with Large Language Models (LLMs) and their role within MIRABELLE. We report on the performance of several LLMs across vital stages of vulnerability detection, from grammatical and technical error-flagging in short phrasings, to complete process structure recovery and extraction.
articles.titleCn: 基于LLM的业务流程文档中的漏洞发现
articles.abstractCn: 与软件和硬件一样，业务流程也容易受到可能导致产品质量问题、延误和成本增加的漏洞的影响。业务流程漏洞可能源于多种来源，包括冲突的需求、模糊的文档、无效的测量规范、遗漏质量检查或与规范不一致的实施。MIRABELLE是一个系统，它可以从可用的业务流程表示中识别和描述业务逻辑（BL）漏洞，包括ISO 9000/9001文档、用户指南、工作指令和流程执行日志。MIRABELLE利用人工智能/机器学习领域的最新进展来处理可用的业务流程文档，并生成业务逻辑的属性图表示，这些表示可以使用图和形式逻辑方法来识别潜在的漏洞。然而，由于需要领域专业知识、固有的流程复杂性以及有时非常大的信息量，从主要自然语言工件中提取业务逻辑（例如，操作执行序列、决策、输入/输出资源）具有挑战性。本文重点介绍我们对大型语言模型（LLMs）的实验及其在MIRABELLE中的作用。我们报告了几个LLMs在漏洞检测的关键阶段的表现，从短语的语法和技术错误标记到完整流程结构的恢复和提取。

articles.title: The Fairness Collapse Phenomenon: Bias Amplification in Language Models Trained on Synthetic Data
articles.abstract: Generative models trained on artificially generated data have been shown to exhibit model collapse, resulting in significant performance degradation. As synthetic content increasingly contaminates the training corpora of language models, this raises critical concerns about the use of open data in continued pretraining. Although previous work has demonstrated model collapse in language models, it remains unclear whether exposure to synthetic data amplifies or attenuates the social biases already present in pretrained models. Because language models are known to reproduce and amplify demographic stereotypes, recursive training on self-generated data may create a self-reinforcing feedback loop in which biased associations become progressively stronger across generations. We call this hypothesized phenomenon fairness collapse. In this work, we construct controlled training regimes in which models are repeatedly trained on synthetic data using the Bias in Bios dataset. Across experiments, we observe a consistent and concerning pattern: fairness degradation emerges before substantial degradation is reflected by standard language-modeling metrics. This result highlights a critical risk associated with synthetic data contamination in language model training: bias can increase silently before strong indicators of model collapse become apparent.
articles.titleCn: 合成数据训练的语言模型中的偏差放大现象：公平性崩溃现象
articles.abstractCn: 在人工生成数据上训练的生成模型已被证明会出现模型坍塌现象，导致性能显著下降。随着合成内容越来越多地污染语言模型的训练语料库，这引发了关于在持续预训练中使用开放数据的重大担忧。尽管以往的研究已经证明语言模型会出现模型坍塌现象，但目前尚不清楚接触合成数据会放大还是减弱预训练模型中已存在的社交偏见。由于语言模型已知会复制和放大人口统计学刻板印象，对自我生成数据进行递归训练可能会形成一个自我强化的反馈循环，其中偏见关联在代际间变得越来越强。我们将这种现象假定为“公平坍塌”。在本工作中，我们构建了受控的训练机制，其中模型使用Bias in Bios数据集反复在合成数据上进行训练。在各项实验中，我们观察到一种持续且令人担忧的模式：公平性退化在标准语言模型指标反映出显著退化之前就已出现。这一结果突显了语言模型训练中合成数据污染所关联的关键风险：偏见可能在模型坍塌的明显指标出现之前悄无声息地增加。

articles.title: Towards End-to-End Multilingual Metaphor Processing: Integrating Detection, Translation, and Evaluation
articles.abstract: Metaphorical language remains a major challenge for multilingual natural language processing because successful interpretation and translation require reasoning beyond literal lexical meaning. Existing research has largely investigated metaphor detection, machine translation, and translation evaluation as separate tasks, while little work has explored how these components can be integrated into a unified computational framework. This PhD proposal aims to develop an end-to-end framework for multilingual metaphor processing consisting of three complementary research directions: (1) robust metaphor detection across languages, (2) metaphor-oriented translation evaluation for both human assessment and automatic quality estimation, and (3) joint modelling that connects metaphor detection with translation evaluation. The proposed research will combine linguistic theory with recent advances in large language models to develop new datasets, annotation methodologies, evaluation benchmarks, and automatic evaluation approaches for metaphor-aware machine translation. The expected outcome is a unified framework that improves both the development and evaluation of multilingual NLP systems when processing figurative language.
